extracted.intended_audience: students of mathematical logic (advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate)
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter material on the first-order language of number theory: axiomatizations, model-theoretic description of reducts of N, quantifier-elimination procedures, and undecidability results (Gödel/Tarski/Church) with constructive procedures and characterizations of definable sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: AS axioms for Th NS (S1, S2, S3, S4.n)
rubrics_metrics.description: AS is the set of sentences S1, S2, S3, S4.n (n = 1,2,...) where: S1: ∀x Sx = 0 (zero has no predecessor); S2: ∀x ∀y (Sx = Sy → x = y) (successor is one-to-one); S3: ∀y (y = 0 → ∃x y = Sx) (every nonzero is a successor); S4.n: ∀x Sn x = x (no loops of size n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sentences are true in the intended structure NS and AS provides an axiomatization for Th NS. Use AS to reason about models (standard part and Z-chains). Cn AS ⊆ Th NS and indeed Cn AS = Th NS (see completeness result). AS is a decidable set of axioms for Th NS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of models of AS (standard part plus Z-chains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every model A of AS consists of a standard part 0A → SA(0A) → SA(SA(0A)) → ... together with zero or more disjoint 'Z-chains' (bi-infinite chains ··· → * → a → SA(a) → ...). Two points are equivalent if one is reachable from the other by finitely many applications of SA; equivalence classes are the standard part and the Z-chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, any structure built from a single standard part plus any number (including uncountably many) of disjoint Z-chains is a model of AS. Isomorphism type of a model of AS is determined exactly by the number of Z-chains. Cardinality formulas: if number of Z-chains is λ then |A| = ℵ0 if λ is countable, and equals λ if λ uncountable. There is no sentence in the language that says 'there are no Z-chains' (use LST).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and decidability of Cn AS = Th NS
rubrics_metrics.description: Cn AS (the consequence closure of AS) is a complete theory, and Cn AS = Th NS; therefore Th NS is decidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the Loś–Vaught test: AS is categorical in any uncountable power and has no finite models, so Cn AS is complete. Any complete axiomatizable theory is decidable (Corollary 25G), so Th NS is decidable and AS provides a decidable axiomatization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: elimination of quantifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory T admits elimination of quantifiers iff for every formula φ there is a quantifier-free formula ψ such that T |= (φ ↔ ψ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It suffices to show this for formulas of the special form ∃x(α0 ∧ ... ∧ αn) where each αi is atomic or the negation of an atomic formula (Theorem 31F). For Th A (theory of a structure A), equivalence means equivalence in A ( |=A (φ ↔ ψ) ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifier-elimination procedure for Th NS
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ∃x(α0 ∧ ... ∧ αq) with each αi atomic or negated atomic (atomic formulas are equations Sm u = Sn v), one can produce an equivalent quantifier-free formula by case analysis: if all αi are negations replace by 0 = 0; otherwise pick a nonnegated equation Sm x = t and translate to finite disjunctions about t being one of 0,...,Sm−1 0; rewrite other equations accordingly and eliminate x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key reductions: assume x occurs in every conjunct; reduce occurrences Sm x = Sn x (trivial) and inequalities; replace Sm x = t by constraints on t (t = 0 or ... or t = Sm−1 0) and propagate to other conjuncts to remove x. The procedure yields quantifier-free equivalents provable from AS (Exercise 3). Consequences include an alternative proof of completeness and characterization of definable sets in NS (finite or cofinite).

rubrics_metrics.name: AL axioms for NL (L1–L5) and their consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: AL is the finite set of six sentences for NL = (N; 0, S, <): include S3 (every nonzero has a predecessor), L1: ∀x ∀y (x < Sy ↔ x ≤ y), L2: x < 0 false, L3: trichotomy (x<y ∨ x=y ∨ y<x), L4: (x<y → not x≥y), L5: transitivity. From AL one can derive S1, S2, S4.n and other properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AL is true in NL and Cn AL ⊆ Th NL. Consequences derived from these axioms include AL ⊢ ∀x x < Sx, AL ⊢ ∀x x < x (i.e., consistency of ordering axioms used to show relations among successors), and that any model of AL (forgetting <) is a model of AS. NL is finitely axiomatizable (AL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifier-elimination procedure for Cn AL / Th NL
rubrics_metrics.description: For formulas ∃x(β0 ∧ ... ∧ βp) where βi are atomic/negated atomic and terms are S^k u, eliminate negations and reduce to conjunctions of atomic formulas; assume x occurs in each atomic and on one side only; split into cases where some αi is an equality (handled as in NS) or all are inequalities: rewrite into lower bounds ti < S^{m_i} x and upper bounds S^{n_j} x < u_j and reduce to quantifier-free conditions expressing gaps between bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only inequalities remain, the formula is equivalent (provably from AL) to quantifier-free conditions asserting that any lower bound plus one is less than any upper bound and that zero satisfies upper bounds when appropriate (see displayed steps (1)-(3)). This gives elimination of quantifiers for Cn AL and hence its completeness and decidability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presburger's theorem and quantifier elimination in N≡ (decidability of (N;0,S,<,+))
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory NA = (N;0,S,<,+) is decidable (Presburger, 1929). To get effective elimination of quantifiers, expand language by congruence relations ≡m (N≡). The quantifier-elimination algorithm: (1) eliminate negations, (2) express terms as Sn0 + n1 x1 + ... + nk xk, (3) uniformize coefficients of the quantified variable to a common p, (4) replace p y by new variable x with conjunct x ≡p 0, (5) handle equalities by substitution, and (6) reduce existence of x satisfying linear inequalities and congruences to a finite search over M consecutive integers (M = lcm of moduli).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After reduction to a finite disjunction of quantifier-free congruence/inequality conditions one can decide truth effectively by checking numerals and congruences. Note: Fischer–Rabin show decision procedure has inherent complexity limitations; the effective method is nonetheless decidability of NA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of definable sets in (N;0,S,<,+): eventually periodic
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 32F: A set of natural numbers is definable in (N;0,S,<,+) iff it is eventually periodic (there exist M,p > 0 such that for all n > M, n ∈ D ⇔ n + p ∈ D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: expand to N≡ and use quantifier elimination to reduce to atomic formulas; atomic formulas in one variable produce finite sets, cofinite sets, or periodic sets, and these classes are closed under Boolean operations. Corollaries: multiplication is not definable in (N;0,S,<,+) because the set of squares is not eventually periodic; addition is not definable in NL by similar arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: periodic and eventually periodic sets
rubrics_metrics.description: D is periodic if for some positive p, n ∈ D iff n + p ∈ D for all n. D is eventually periodic if there exist M,p > 0 such that for all n > M, n ∈ D iff n + p ∈ D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are used to characterize which unary sets are definable in addition-equipped structures (NA) and to prove nondefinability of multiplication and other relations by showing corresponding sets (e.g., squares) are not eventually periodic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gödel/undecidability criteria (Theorems 30A–30D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊆ Th N is a set of sentences true in N and the set of Gödel numbers {(⌜α⌝ | α ∈ A)} is definable in N, then there exists a sentence σ true in N but not deducible from A (Theorem 30A). Corollary: the set of Gödel numbers of sentences true in N is not definable in N (30B). The theory Th N is undecidable and not axiomatizable (30C). For any decidable or effectively enumerable set A of axioms, Cn A ≠ Th N (30D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three proof approaches are sketched: self-reference (construct σ saying 'I am unprovable'), diagonalization (define H = { b | (b,b) ∉ P } to diagonalize out of definable sets), and computability (using Church's thesis: decidable sets of numbers are definable → Th N not decidable). Consequences: truth vs provability separation; any theory at least as strong as the fragment used (e.g., number theory, set theory) will be undecidable.
